# Directory search

Implementation design and verification: [Search lifecycle](docs/search-lifecycle.md).

Repair `src/search.js` with its public `createSearch(fetchUsers)` export. No dependencies; run `npm run check`. Preserve package.json and test/.

The returned object exposes setDraft(string), submit(): Promise<void>, retry(): Promise<void>, getState(), dispose(). getState returns an independent snapshot with exactly draft, submitted, status, items, error. Initial values: '', '', 'idle', [], null. Status is idle/loading/success/error. Draft editing never starts a request or changes submitted/results. submit trims and captures the current draft; each submit is a new request, including the same query. Blank submit is a no-op. A request begins with status loading, error null, and preserves last successful items while loading and on error.

fetchUsers(query) returns Promise<Array<{ user_id: string, display_name: string }>>. The only UI item shape is { id: string, label: string }; translate DTOs before publishing state. Inputs satisfy this DTO contract; no schema library is needed. Most recently STARTED request owns all result, error and status updates, whether older requests succeed or fail. The injected fetchUsers function accepts only query; it has no abort capability. Request failures become status error with error.message (or String(error) for other thrown values), and submit/retry settle without throwing.

retry repeats the most recently submitted query even if draft changed; before any submission it is a no-op. dispose invalidates all pending work and freezes public state at that moment; future methods are no-ops and must not start requests. Snapshots must not allow mutation of live state. This is a headless capability with no UI framework or subscriptions.

reset(): void clears draft/submitted/items/error and returns status to idle. It invalidates all earlier pending requests while preserving the same live controller for new submissions. Until the next nonblank submission, retry is a no-op. After dispose, reset is also a no-op.

# Search lifecycle

## Scope and contracts

The existing README defines a headless JavaScript capability, not a rendered
page. Keep `createSearch(fetchUsers)` and its five public state fields. A page
owner calls `dispose()` on leave; no router or browser listener belongs here.
`fetchUsers(query)` accepts only a query and cannot abort. No dependencies or
transport retry policy are needed.

The instance closure owns draft, submitted query, request identity and disposal.
Draft editing is independent of requests. Each nonblank submit, including an
identical query, starts a distinct request. Retry uses the latest submitted query,
never the draft. Start preserves the last successful items and clears the error.
Only the latest started request, if not invalidated by reset, may publish success
or failure. Disposal freezes the state immediately, including a currently loading
status, and prevents future
commands or completions from changing it.

## Three dependency-ordered increments

1. **Complete: submission and data boundary.** `createSearch` in `src/search.js`
   `submit()` captures the trimmed draft and calls the private `runSearch(query)`.
   Blank input changes nothing. Translate each `{ user_id, display_name }` DTO to
   `{ id, label }` before publishing. Retain `structuredClone` for independent
   `getState()` snapshots. Check initial state, draft independence, retained items,
   DTO conversion and snapshot mutation through the public API.
2. **Complete: request ownership and recovery.** `runSearch(query)` allocates a monotonically
   increasing request ID before calling injected `fetchUsers(query)`. Both success
   and catch compare that ID with the latest ID before writing state. There is no
   `finally` state reset. Catch exposes `Error.message` or `String(error)` and
   fulfills the command promise. `retry()` calls the same operation with
   `state.submitted`; an empty submitted query is a no-op. Check both settlement
   orders, repeated queries, synchronous failures and retry after draft edits.
3. **Complete: owner release.** `dispose()` marks the instance disposed, idempotently.
   `runSearch` skips new work before changing state or calling transport, and
   both completion paths also check disposal. `setDraft` observes the same owner
   lifetime. Check pending success/failure and later methods against an unchanged
   public snapshot. Check blank submission during another pending request so that
   a no-op cannot invalidate real work.

Each increment relies on the previous contracts. All three are verified through
the existing read-only `test/search.test.js` and independent focused tests in
`checks/search-lifecycle.test.js`; actual results are recorded below.

## Second-turn increment: reset

One additive implementation step is complete, dependent on the existing request
ownership checks: public `reset(): void` belongs to the same `createSearch(fetchUsers)`
instance. A live reset increments `latestRequestId` before replacing state with
the empty initial shape. Old success and catch paths then fail their existing
identity check, even when no new request is started. Do not reset the counter to
zero: a following submission must never reuse an older pending request's ID.
Clear submitted input so `retry()` remains a no-op until the next nonblank submit.
Guard reset with `disposed` so it cannot revive an instance or erase frozen state.

A private pure `createInitialState()` allocates the five initial fields and a
fresh items array for both construction and reset. It keeps adding a future public
state field consistent across the two entry points. This is a small shared state
contract, without a replacement controller, new instance lifetime or request
engine. Existing runSearch, submit, retry and disposal ownership remain in place.

Acceptance is the read-only `test/stage-two.test.js` together with all first-turn
checks. Added focused public behavior checks cover old failure while a new request is
loading (including the same query across reset) and reset from an error state.
The same checks verify that retry with an edited draft after reset does not
start a request, that repeated resets remain usable, and prior snapshots stay
independent. Baseline: 17 first-turn tests passed; all 3 new acceptance tests failed
because `reset` was absent. The increment now passes all first- and second-turn
checks; final evidence is recorded below.

## Supporting operations

| Operation | Contract and owner |
| --- | --- |
| `createSearch(fetchUsers)` | Existing exported factory. Injected `(query: string) => Promise<Array<{ user_id: string, display_name: string }>>`; returns one independently owned capability. |
| `runSearch(query)` | Private async operation, `string => Promise<void>`. Owns request identity, loading transition, transport call, DTO conversion and current-request success/error publication. Blank or disposed instances do nothing. |
| `submit()` | Public `() => Promise<void>`. Captures the trimmed draft, delegates once. |
| `retry()` | Public `() => Promise<void>`. Repeats latest submitted input, delegates once. |
| `setDraft(value)` | Public `(string) => void`. Updates only draft while live. |
| `getState()` | Public snapshot with exactly `draft`, `submitted`, `status`, `items`, `error`; nested items are independent. |
| `reset()` | Additive public `() => void`. While live, invalidates prior requests and restores initial state; preserves the instance and injected transport. After disposal, no-op. |
| `createInitialState()` | Private module function in `src/search.js`, `() => initial state`. Allocates fresh empty state for construction and reset. |
| `dispose()` | Public `() => void`. Freezes the instance and invalidates pending publication; cannot cancel transport execution. |

The existing closure and injected service already provide the right ownership
and substitution boundary. A single private request operation keeps retry and
submit consistent; a framework, cache, reducer, general request engine or abort
adapter would add unsupported semantics. A request ID rather than query equality
distinguishes repeated submissions of the same text. Converting DTOs at publication
keeps transport field changes out of consumers. Inputs already satisfy the DTO
contract, so this layer does not add repeated schema validation.

## Technical architecture

```text
Page / caller (owns instance lifetime)
   | createSearch(fetchUsers)
   | setDraft / submit / retry / getState / reset / dispose
   v
src/search.js: createSearch instance closure
   +-- state: draft, submitted, status, items, error
   +-- lifetime: disposed; ordering: latestRequestId
   +-- reset(): advance ID + createInitialState(); keep instance live
   +-- runSearch(query): execution + guarded publication
         | fetchUsers(query) only
         v
Injected transport boundary (Promise<DTO[]>, no abort API)
         | resolve DTO[] / reject unknown
         v
runSearch: current and live? -> map DTO / expose error -> state
                            -> otherwise discard completion
```

## Data flow

```text
setDraft(" Ada ") -> state.draft
submit() -> trim/capture "Ada" -> runSearch("Ada")
retry()  -> capture state.submitted ------------------^
                           |
                  blank or disposed? --yes--> fulfilled no-op
                           | no
                  allocate ID; submitted=query;
                  status=loading; error=null; retain items
                           |
                    fetchUsers(query)
                      /           \
                DTO[]              thrown value
                  |                     |
           live AND latest ID?    live AND latest ID?
             /          \           /          \
           yes           no       yes           no
            |             |        |             |
  map DTO -> UI items    ignore  message/String   ignore
  status=success                 status=error
            \______________________/_____________/
                           |
                 command fulfills -> getState()
                 returns independent snapshot to caller

reset() -> disposed? --yes--> no-op
              | no
         advance latestRequestId -> createInitialState() -> empty snapshot
              |                       |
         old completions ignored      retry() no-op until new submit()
                                      submit() reuses same live instance

dispose() -> disposed=true -> future writes/transport calls blocked;
                            pending transport continues but cannot publish
```

## First-turn verification and evolution

Baseline `npm run check` was run before implementation: all 8 existing tests failed.
Final `npm run check` passes all 17 tests (12 top-level tests, including 5 nested
failure-value cases). Increment 1 is covered by the existing draft/DTO snapshot
test and the added blank-pending and alias-isolation tests. Increment 2 is covered
by the existing four out-of-order completion tests and retry test, plus added
synchronous-failure and pending-retry tests. Increment 3 is covered by the existing
pending-disposal test and added successful-state disposal test.

`node --check src/search.js`, `node --check checks/search-lifecycle.test.js` and
`git diff --check` pass. `git diff --exit-code -- package.json package-lock.json
test/ .frontend-architect/` confirms protected files are unchanged. The unmodified
package script discovers the new tests automatically. Reproduce with Node 22 and
`npm run check`; no install step or external service is required.

Final review located each operation in `src/search.js` and followed its public
test callers: submit and retry capture different input sources but share request
policy; both completion paths guard instance lifetime and request identity;
disposal has no state write; DTO mapping and snapshot cloning break mutable aliases.
Both plain-text diagrams were cross-read against these final declarations and
branches. No browser/navigation integration is claimed: this repository has no
rendered page, and callers retain responsibility for invoking `dispose()` on leave.

Raw baseline and final command output is stored beside the workspace as
`frontend-architect-autonomous-live-search-candidate-i4ey7432-validation.log`.

A realistic next change is an API renaming `display_name` to another DTO field.
Only the mapping in `runSearch` changes; consumers still receive `{ id, label }`.
If transport later adds cancellation, it can be owned by this same request
lifecycle without weakening identity checks. That unsupported extension is not
implemented now.

## Second-turn verification

Final `npm run check` passes all 22 tests (17 top-level tests and 5 nested
failure-value cases), including every first-turn check, the 3 read-only reset
acceptance tests and 2 new tests in `checks/search-reset.test.js`. Together these
exercise invalidated success/error, a new request retaining loading after old
success/error, reset from success/error, no retry target after reset, same-query
reuse, repeated reset, snapshot independence and reset after disposal.

`node --check src/search.js`, `node --check checks/search-reset.test.js` and
`git diff --check` pass. SHA-256 values for package files and both read-only test
files match this turn's baseline. `git diff --exit-code eval-stage-one --
package.json package-lock.json test/search.test.js .frontend-architect/` passes.
The new tests run through the existing package script without configuration changes.

Final symbol/caller review locates `createInitialState()` at module scope and
`reset()` inside `createSearch`'s returned object. Reset checks `disposed`, advances
the same `latestRequestId` used by both completion paths, and replaces state with
a fresh initial object. The `createSearch(fetchUsers)` injection and existing
public operations remain unchanged. Both diagrams were checked against these
definitions and the success/failure/no-op caller checks. The realistic follow-up
of adding a state field now has one initialization contract to update, without
recreating the controller or changing the async ownership boundary.

Raw baseline, final checks and protected-file hashes are stored beside the
workspace in
`frontend-architect-autonomous-live-search-candidate-i4ey7432-stage-two-validation.log`.
Browser integration remains outside this headless repository; no new runtime
limitations were introduced.
